independent_findings.threshold: Distance integrality and bound D=n−1 imply w(u)d<=R iff d<=max{k<=D:k w(u)<=R}; complement labels D−b are nonnegative integers <=D. Zero labels and equality survive. Taking max yields full feasible set, including all-zero and singleton cases.
independent_findings.search: Each radius is a candidate k w(u). Feasible incumbent plus active-optimum invariant survives either weak deletion. A weighted median of lower-middle row entries removes >=M/4 multiplicity, including L=1, L=2 and ties. At most O(log n) queries, O(n log^2 n) comparison overhead.
independent_findings.BDH_structure: Read §§2–4. Gated halfspace/slice identities do not require a specific f beyond >=2. Both original and fiber labels are needed. Basepoint-farthest self tie returns via triangle inequality. For disjoint ladders, the median m(v0,v,umax) gives a direct independent argument: if m≠v0 its first edge supplies a shared incident separating class; contradiction. Then v0 is on a geodesic and gives additive eccentricity.
independent_findings.recursion_corrections: For f(s)=2 ceil(log2 s), ladder length ell<=log2 s<=ceil(log2 s), and two copies of disjoint slices total <=2 ell s/f<=s. Child size <=s(1−1/f). Since f(s)<=4 log2 s, root-bound factor 1−1/(lambda ln N), lambda=4/ln2, proves O(log^2 N) depth without wrong endpoint product. O(s log^2 s) local work times per-level volume N gives O(N log^4 N). Labels bounded by initial max + depth*(N−1), hence O(log N) bits.
